title: Camp Pendleton Wildfire Report
description: Package of the spread and treatment of wildfires in San Diego County, California and how evacuees are being helped though the Marines. Produced by Cpl. Stephen Holt.
keywords: Gunnery Sgt. Scott Becherer, Col. James Seaton

transcript.text: It's a scene being repeated over and over throughout the Southern California landscape,
wildfires scorching thousands of acres and leaving nothing behind in their wake.
Approximately 500,000 San Diego County residents are being asked by county officials to leave
their homes behind and head for safer ground away from the raging wildfires.
One area heavily affected by the spreading inferno is the city of Fallbrook, an area that
is home to many Marines and sailors based out of nearby Marine Corps-based Camp Pendleton.
As the fires moved into the area Monday, all service members and civilians living in Fallbrook
were told to evacuate immediately.
Camp Pendleton officials saw this as an opportunity to reach out to their neighbors in need by
opening up Camp Pendleton's gates and allowing people to pass through the base safely.
We're all neighbors.
The bulk of our married Marines live off base in the local communities, so one might tend
to think of Camp Pendleton as where all the Marines are, but again we've got thousands
and thousands of Marines and sailors and family members in the local communities.
So we are linked to them.
We're linked in everything we do.
On top of that, the installation also provided more than 2,100 cots and other essential
goods for San Diego residents in need.
We're taking in civilians, we've taken in retired Marines, we've taken in active duty
Marines.
Basically anybody has been misplaced because of the fires that are going on in San Diego
County currently.
We provided food services here at the 14 area Taul Hall as well.
We provided waters, you know, to these people who have been misplaced.
So all in all it's just a good thing for the community whether it be both military
and or civilian.
However, as the week moved along and fires continued to spread, Camp Pendleton itself was
hit by a wildfire outbreak.
A fire broke out near Camp Margarita and another in Camp Horno.
Emergency workers continue to work hard day and night to completely stomp out the spread
of the fires.
Camp Pendleton residents are encouraged to tune into K-Pen channel 18, call the information
hotline at area code 866-430-2764 or check the Camp Pendleton website for the most current
and up-to-date information.
Reporting from Marine Corps Base Camp Pendleton, I'm Marine Corporal Stephen Holt.
